driver: The decisive quantity is a rare-event level at an unmeasured unit transferred from a measured neighbour whose events each drew on only the part of it below a threshold that moved from event to event, while the unmeasured unit lies almost wholly below that threshold: transferring by size undersizes it, a ratio read at a typical event oversizes it because the largest events drew on nearly all of the neighbour, and only transferring every event at its own threshold lands the level.
driver_concrete: The Coyner River's floods drain rain only below each storm's snow line, a median half of its high basin and three fifths in its largest floods, while Durrow Creek's foothill basin drains whole in almost every storm; carried by drainage area the river's record files 18,700 cfs and the 140 ft span, carried flood by flood at the ratio of the two basins' storm rain below the snow line (placed by the stations' storm lapse rate and the snow pillows' rain-snow temperature, with the orographic rise) it files 27,200 cfs and the 185 ft span, and the same carry with the textbook lapse rate or without the orographic rise files the 240 ft span.
stump: A strong analyst carries the Coyner River's Bulletin 17C curve to Durrow Creek by drainage area, back-tests it between the region's high gauges and builds the 140 ft span on about 18,700 cfs; only carrying every flood at the ratio of the two basins' storm rain below its snow line, placed from the stations, files about 27,200 cfs and the 185 ft span, and the textbook lapse rate files the 240 ft span.
deep_chain: (1) the river's floods drain only the area below each storm's snow line, placed storm by storm from the valley and SNOTEL temperatures with the storm lapse rate; (2) the creek's basin lies below that line in nearly every storm, so its rain-contributing area per storm is a different function of the snow line from the river's; (3) the transfer factor varies by storm and is smallest for the warm storms behind the river's largest floods, so every storm is transferred at its own snow line, never at a typical one; (4) the frequency curve of the creek's transferred annual series gives its 1 per cent flood and the span
judgment: the response model linking each storm's flood to its rain-contributing volume (rain over the area below the snow line, with the orographic gradient the stations show), fitted on the river's events against the drainage-area model, and the snow line itself (the storm lapse rate from valley and SNOTEL pairs, the rain-snow temperature from the SNOTEL record's rain and snow days)
one_fact_test: 'the creek is rain-dominated' rescues nothing: the transfer must still be built storm by storm from the station temperatures, a lapse rate and both basins' elevation bands, and the single representative ratio that sentence invites files the 240 ft span

lineage.driver: The extra input an upgraded service level puts into a unit is the part of the unit the old level left untreated, so the average gain measured on units upgraded earlier, chosen because the old level already treated much of them, understates the gain for units the old level barely reached, while their upgraded level less the new units' present input overstates it; only the gain conditioned on how much of each unit the old level already treated, read from each unit's own record under it, carries across to the new units.
lineage.stump: A competent solver takes the Priority 1 collectors' salt per lane-km per severity point less the 424 lane-km's own Priority 2 salt and files 2,600 t at the planning severity, or takes the before-and-after gain of the collectors moved to Priority 1 since 2022 and files 1,500 to 1,600 t; the step that lands it there is carrying an average across streets whose Priority 2 coverage differs, when the gain is the length Priority 2 left untreated and the earlier moves were mostly hill, school and inner-suburb streets Priority 2 had already salted along much of their length, so only the gain conditioned on each street's own Priority 2 salt files 2,200 t.
lineage.driver_concrete: Quellbrook's Priority 2 trucks salt a collector only at its intersections, hills and curves, so a collector's gain on moving to Priority 1 is mostly the stretch between them at the Priority 1 rate; the collectors moved from 2022 to 2025 were mostly hill, school and hospital-access streets whose Priority 2 salt already covered much of their length, while the redesign's 424 lane-km are long flat outer-suburb grid collectors whose Priority 2 trucks salted about a sixth of them, so the moved streets' average gain understates theirs and the Priority 1 collectors' rate less the new streets' own Priority 2 salt overstates it; only the gain read off each moved street's own Priority 2 salt, at the new streets' Priority 2 salt, carries across.
lineage.fate: landed on the portal (2026-11-07): one response filed the golden 2,200 t by regressing each earlier move's gain on its own Priority 2 salt and reading it at the new streets' (100 per cent), the other filed the default 2,600 t and still kept 70 per cent on the asks; conditioning a carried gain on a covariate each unit's history prints is the strong solver's reflex, so the world is spent

lineage.driver: A storage buffer that captures a discharge until it is full empties only through a receiving channel whose spare capacity vanishes for one to several days after each wet event, so in a run of events the buffer meets the next one still partly full; counting each event against an empty buffer, or a buffer emptied at its outlet's rated pace, understates how often it spills, and only replaying the record with the outlet bounded by the receiving channel's spare capacity, read from that channel's own record, prices the size the limit needs.
lineage.driver_concrete: Clay Street's tank is pumped out into the Southside interceptor at the plant headworks, and the Southside plant, its sewershed full of groundwater and inflow, takes its 140 MGD hydraulic limit for one to four days after most storms from March to June; the Northside tank, whose plant has room within hours, empties at its pumps' rating and its overflows replay exactly that way, but Clay Street's pumps can only send what Southside has room for, so in a wet spell the tank meets the next storm still full and the 26 MG alternative that clears four events at its pumps' rating leaves 6.8 a year; only the 38 MG tank, at 2.9, meets the decree.
lineage.stump: A competent solver replays Outfall 014's metered overflows through each tank pumped out at its station's rated dewatering flow (the continuous simulation the decree evaluates by, which reproduces the Northside tank's overflows since 2020) and selects Alternative B, the 26 MG tank, at 2.8 events a year; the step that lands it there is taking the pumps' rating as the pace the tank empties, when it empties into the Southside interceptor at the headworks of a plant that sits at its 140 MGD limit for days after wet-season storms, so only a replay bounded by Southside's own headroom hour by hour shows the 20 MG tank at 6.8 events and selects Alternative C, the 38 MG tank, at 2.9.
lineage.answer: Select Alternative C, the 38 MG tank: it leaves Outfall 014 2.9 untreated overflow events a year, where the 26 MG Alternative B leaves 6.8.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a long-horizon response to a sustained load, when a short trial's response carries two opposing far-field effects that cancel inside its window and part only over years: the trial's own model fits it closely and overstates the long response, so the far field must be calibrated on the record a nearby load has already left, read against a natural baseline from references beyond that load's reach, because the nearest reference sits inside it and a fitted trend absorbs the response.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each requested rate's greatest monthly drawdown at OW-S in 2046 from a bounded leaky aquifer whose leakage factor is calibrated on the drawdown the Mill Street wells caused at MS-MW and OW-S from 2009 to 2026, each well's natural level carried from the far network wells CV-02 and CV-11; not the 72-hour test's Theis fit extrapolated, and not a calibration against the readings' own pre-pumping levels, the nearest network well CV-07 (inside the Mill Street cone) or a fitted trend, each of which credits the region's wet years to leakage.
lineage.stump: A strong analyst who sees the test's Theis forecast overshoot the Mill Street record recalibrates the leakage against the nearest network well CV-07 (or the wells' own pre-pumping levels, or a fitted trend) and files 1,250 gpm, every schedule under 3.5 ft at OW-S; only the natural level carried from CV-02 and CV-11 beyond the cone files 1,000 gpm.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a blended output's level over the coming years, fed by inputs whose change at the source travels through a stage no measurement of the output or of the medium sees, at a pace set by each source's own depth through that stage; a recent change sits on sources deeper than the earlier changes that matured, so the output's own history, one delay fitted to it, the downstream travel time a filed model gives, and an event study on the recent change all show no effect and set it near nil, and only the matured changes' delays, read against each source's depth and carried to each recent source, show the rise arriving inside the decision window.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each year's 2027 to 2040 entry-point nitrate is the pumping plan's blend of Wells 3, 5, 6 and 7, each a recharge-weighted mix of its protection-area parcels' water-table nitrate delayed by the wellhead model's groundwater travel time, where a parcel's water-table nitrate is its land cover's leachate delayed by its unsaturated thickness times the sand's moisture over the recharge; the Sallow Ridge parcels cleared for irrigated vegetables from 2017 to 2021 sit over 57 to 94 ft of sand, so their leachate reaches the wells late in 2030, not by 2024 as the travel time or the wells' own lag would put it.
lineage.stump: A strong analyst who finds the ridge clearing tests it against the wells and the county wells under recent clearings, sees no rise where the wellhead model's travel time or the wells' own fitted lag says it should already be, sets the clearing's effect near nil and files the 2031 cycle with the blend near 5.5 mg/L through 2040; only each parcel's delay through its own unsaturated thickness, read from the county's older conversions, puts the rise at the wells late in 2030 and the blend at 10 in 2031.
